messages:
Maya: thinking out loud — I'm prototyping a 'gradual-throttle' downscaling policy to avoid painful KV-cache cold starts for models with long-lived context. idea: instead of immediate drain after idle threshold, we step down node capacity in stages and mark nodes as 'preserve-kv' if they've served >X active sessions.
Ethan: sounds promising. what's the heuristic for 'long-lived'? session count or time since last activation?
Maya: leaning toward a hybrid: keep nodes with >3 active sessions OR last-active < 20m and total kvsize > 1GB. that avoids keeping nodes warm for tiny demos.
Priya: cost check — if we keep ~10% of the fleet warm in eu-west1 that adds ~0.8k/mo for our current fleet, is that acceptable? also need to ensure we don't block scale-to-zero for test clusters.
Maya: yes we can scope per-cluster and have a config flag. default: only enable on prod pools (nodepool label: "scale.policy=gradual-preserve").
Jon: operational question: how will this interact with cluster-autoscaler? will we annotate nodes or use a custom controller?
Maya: plan is controller that intercepts scale decisions and introduces a 3-step cooldown: 1) soft-evict (mark pod priority), 2) cordon + delay 5m, 3) drain if still idle. controller also toggles a node annotation `redwood.dev/kv-preserve=true` to signal lower-priority autoscaler eviction.
Maya: sample annotation snippet we tested locally:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
metadata:
  name: gw-gpu-03
  annotations:
    redwood.dev/kv-preserve: "true"
```
Ethan: instead of node annotation can we use node groups + taints? preserving a few nodes via tolerations seems cleaner and avoids autoscaler conflicts.
Priya: tolerations = fine but we still need a way to prefer scale-down of on-demand vs spot. keep warm on on-demand only? that'd be pricey.
Claire: region constraint — in eu-west we already have scarcity on on-demand. my worry: if warm nodes are only on-demand, we could create imbalance during AZ failures. maybe allow warm on mixed instances but prefer cheapest with fast warmup.
Jon: also consider KV eviction safety: if we keep nodes for KV, we must ensure the runtime persists checkpoint to S3 within 2h in case of preemption. else we'll leak state.
Maya: agree. adding a background shard-flush that triggers at step 2 (cordon + flush request) — if flush fails, escalate and mark node for immediate drain & reprovision.
autoscaler-bot: noticed a spike in unaccounted GPU allocations in eu-west1: +12% in last 6h. flagged for ops.
Priya: linking cost dashboard here: https://dash.redwood.local/fleet/cost?range=30d — we can model incremental cost by simulating retention percentages.
Ethan: deployment plan? canary pool first?
Maya: propose a canary: 1 nodepool in us-west2, 1 in eu-west1, 24h canary with metrics: median cold-start latency, per-token cost, and preemption rates. if cold-start latency drops >30% with <1.5x cost, push.
Jon: also add probe for AZ balance — fail if skew > 20% during canary.
Claire: +1 to canary. schedule a quick 30m sync tomorrow to walk the rollout steps and config flags.
Priya: I'll run cost sim and share numbers before sync.
Maya: action items: I’ll push controller PR with basic annotation + cordon/delay logic, Ethan will prototype a toleration variant, Priya runs cost sims, Jon adds S3 flush hook, Claire will pick canary pools.
deploy-bot: queued 1992-gradual-throttle-canary to staging for tests :gear:
Maya: thanks — posting the PR link once it's up. any objections to labeling this as opt-in across clusters?
Ethan: no objections. sounds safe. :thumbsup:
Priya: sounds good.
Jon: ok, talk tomorrow.
